newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council to decide on Mideast debate next week.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council to decide on Mideast debate next week.

text.p: The Security Council will decide next week when to hold a debate requested by the Arab group on Israel's decision to build homes for Jews in East Jerusalem, council President Njuguna Mahugu said on Friday.
Several Council members said privately they did not think a debate would begin before Tuesday at the earliest.
Mahugu, of Kenya, told reporters after private council counsultations: "The timing of such a meeting will be decided on next week, during Poland's presidency of the council."
The presidency rotates monthly and ambassador Zbigniew Wlosowicz of Poland holds the post during March.

Although the Arab group had formally requested an immediate meeting, to stress the urgency of the issue, it was also believed anxious to avoid any distraction during a previously planned visit to Washington by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
He arrives in Washington late Sunday for meetings the following day with President Bill Clinton and other U.S. officials and travels to New York Tuesday evening.

On Wednesday, Arafat will confer with Secretary-General Kofi Annan and hold other meetings before flying to Houston, Texas, to see former President George Bush and former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker and to delivery a lecture at the James Baker Institute for public policy at Rice University.

The Arab group's request for a council meeting was prompted by Israel's decision Wednesday to build 6,500 homes for Jews on a tree-covered hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem that Israel captured during the 1967 Middle East war. It is called Har Homa by Israel and Jabal Abu Ghneim by the Palestinians.
